statement: Two circles of radius 5 touch each other on the outside. A third circle of radius 5 touches both. What is the perimeter of the triangle joining the three centres?

choices.misconception: I used the three radii as the side lengths of the triangle.
I added a diameter to two radii, mixing the two measurements.
I used three diameters and then added a radius for the third contact point.
I used three diameters, which double counts because the sides are centre to centre.

hints: The distance between centres of touching circles is a sum of radii.
Two circles that touch on the outside have centres exactly the sum of their radii apart. Work out one side that way, then use the symmetry of the arrangement.
Each side joins two centres, so each is 5 + 5 = 10, and the triangle is equilateral.

solutions.reliable: When two circles touch externally the distance between centres equals the sum of the radii, here 5 + 5 = 10. All three sides are 10, so the perimeter is 30. The transferable idea: in touching-circle problems, replace every contact with the centre-to-centre distance and the picture becomes a plain polygon.
solutions.elegant: The three centres form an equilateral triangle of side one diameter, so the perimeter is three diameters.

whyOnTest: Converting tangency into centre distances is the whole technique, and the radius-only and diameter-tripled answers are both on offer.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
